item.title: Nesting expanded space
item.content:encoded:
Personally I'm curious what would happen, if someone moved one expanded container into another expanded space.

There was something similar mentioned in the discussion before:

2) If 184 is placed in a wardrobe within a 184-ed house, will it continue internally expanding the house or begin work on the wardrobe? If the latter, can this nesting be done indefinitely?

And the answer was:

2: Yes, it will start to expand the wardrobe. As this thing is unstable, i think if you nested it too much, it'd start to leak into one another…or into the outside.

but I wonder if nesting without active 184 expansion, nesting after both were already expanded would make it more stable, or whether too much nesting would still collapse the stability

item.title: SCP-184=SCP-001?
item.content:encoded:
Okay hear me out. An expedition's audio log was leaked, it revealed an expedition in the SCPS spacecraft that could travel faster than light. While exploring another galaxy the crew discovered that it was an excact copy of the Milky Way. But the earth and stars and other planets where made out of things like magnets, maple syrup, etc. All planets where devoid of life. Every galaxy was like this, but they also encountered anomonalies on planets and in deep open space. Energy turning off and then on, etc. And when one of the crew members gave birth, she gave birth to a huge anomalious rat monster, causing the crew to return to earth, however all crew members where killed, and only the spacecraft was recovered.

Does the galaxy those audio logs describe nit seem like what SCP-184 would make if it just started with earth and continued on, using already made materials and creating anomalies?

After all, what is the easiest way to keep SCP-001 secret? By not classifying it as SCP-001 at all.

item.title: Staff Post - Open
item.content:encoded:
Timer removed. Edits Made. See below.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 72 hours if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

So there is a plenty of crosslink potential with this article, but two particular proposals have come to my attention that I will include below.

The first is a simple inline link to Jack Ike's excellent tale Code Name: The Truth. I propose the following:

Editing this line:

Any structures affected by SCP-184 are to be demolished after review by [DATA EXPUNGED].

To this:

Any structures affected by SCP-184 are to be demolished after review by [ DATA EXPUNGED ].

In this way, we link to this tale without ultimately disrupting the flow of the article, and play of the mystery behind the expungement.

A second proposal for crosslinks comes from the fact that reading how this object created the oddity that was Kowloon City reminds me a lot of the urban pocket dimensions that are: Three Portlands, Backdoor SoHo, and Chūgoku Cellar. Its possible that this anomaly, or one similar to it, was directly responsible for the creation of these spaces. For this reason an interesting set of crosslinks could be included with the addition of the following Addendum:

Addendum 184 - 2: It is currently hypothesized that SCP-184 or an anomaly with an similar effect may be responsible for the creation of Locations of Interest such as Three Portlands, Backdoor SoHo, and Chūgoku Cellar. Investigation into SCP-184 as a potential origin for these spaces is ongoing.

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

item.title: I still want this thing!
item.content:encoded: I really don't care too much about the dangers with this SCP, I think the possible uses for it outweigh them altogether. For example, if you put it in a box made of gold, it would expand the inside of the box and create a ton more gold! Sure, stuff would get weird after a while, but since it only replicates materials inside the structure being expanded, it will always be gold. Obviously this concept would apply to any material, so it is essentially a free ticket to limitless supplies. I just think that the Foundation would realize this pretty quickly and it could be a nice explanation to its seemingly limitless resources.
